blocks.content: The A&N economy is small, service-dominated, and increasingly shaped by two exam-relevant themes: (a) fisheries/coconut-based traditional economy and (b) the strategically important Great Nicobar Island Development Project — currently the single biggest current-affairs-economy story linked to the territory.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Tourism serves as a principal driver for regional economic growth.
The Great Nicobar Island Development Project focuses on holistic socio-economic development.
Connectivity and infrastructure expansion are vital for overall economic integration.

blocks.content: The economy is overwhelmingly tertiary (services)-dominated, led by tourism, government/public administration employment, and trade — a reflection of the territory's small population, limited industrial base and heavy dependence on shipping/air connectivity to the mainland.

Agriculture is limited by terrain and forest cover; coconut and areca nut (betel nut) are the principal plantation crops, alongside paddy, pulses and vegetables grown mainly for local consumption on South Andaman and the Nicobar Islands.

Fisheries is a significant traditional livelihood given the vast Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) around the islands — A&N Islands account for a very large share (about 30%) of India's total EEZ despite the UT's tiny land area, because EEZ is measured 200 nautical miles from the coastline.

cells: ≈ 30% (largest single-territory share, due to 200-nautical-mile EEZ around the archipelago)
Very limited — mainly agro-processing, coir, handicrafts, fisheries-processing

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: 'A&N Islands hold ~30% of India's total Exclusive Economic Zone' despite having a minuscule land area — a favourite counter-intuitive one-liner in economy/geography-crossover questions.

Tourism is the fastest-growing and most visible economic sector, anchored around Port Blair, Havelock (Swaraj Dweep), Neil (Shaheed Dweep) and Ross Island — covered in depth in the dedicated Tourism chapter. The government has pushed island tourism through schemes like SAGARMALA-linked port development and dedicated island tourism master plans.
Great Nicobar Island Development Project (Holistic Development Project)

The Great Nicobar Island Development Project (also referred to as the 'Holistic Development of Great Nicobar Island' project) is the most important current economy/infrastructure topic for A&N in recent competitive exams. It is a mega infrastructure initiative approved by the Government of India, executed primarily via ANIIDCO in partnership with NITI Aayog, envisaging transformation of Great Nicobar into a major strategic and commercial hub in the Indo-Pacific.
The estimated project cost is around ₹72,000 crore, to be implemented in phases up to roughly 2050, and comprises four major components.

cells: International Container Transshipment Terminal (ICTT) at Galathea Bay
Deep-water port to capture transshipment traffic currently handled by Colombo, Singapore and Port Klang; leverages proximity to the Malacca Strait shipping lane
Dual-use (civilian + military) airport to boost connectivity and strategic reach
Planned urban township to support the new population influx and workforce
To meet the energy needs of the new infrastructure and township

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: The project is highly controversial in current affairs due to environmental and tribal-rights concerns — large tracts of tropical rainforest and Galathea Bay's nesting ground for the Giant Leatherback Turtle are affected, and the Shompen PVTG's habitat overlaps the project area. This intersection with Chapters 5 (Tribes) and 7 (Wildlife) is a very common cross-topic question.

items: Analyze the strategic and economic significance of the Great Nicobar Island Development Project.
Understand the economic impact of tourism and connectivity in island development.
Review key infrastructure initiatives driving regional growth in competitive exam questions.
Veer Savarkar International Airport, Port Blair — the main air gateway, upgraded with a new integrated terminal building inaugurated in 2021 to handle greater passenger traffic.
Shipping services connect Port Blair to Kolkata, Chennai and Visakhapatnam on the mainland; inter-island ferry services (government and private) connect major inhabited islands.

The Andaman Trunk Road (ATR) — the primary road artery running through South, Middle and North Andaman, notorious for passing through the Jarawa Tribal Reserve, raising the tribal-rights and 'human safari' concerns discussed in Chapter 3.

Digital connectivity: the Chennai–Andaman & Nicobar Islands submarine Optical Fibre Cable (CANI) project, commissioned in 2020, connects Port Blair and other major islands (Swaraj Dweep, Shaheed Dweep, Kamorta, Car Nicobar, Little Andaman, Long Island, Rangat, Mayabunder, Diglipur) to high-speed broadband for the first time.
Economy is services-dominated; coconut and areca nut are the main plantation crops.
A&N Islands hold ≈30% of India's total EEZ, the single largest territorial share.
Great Nicobar Island Development Project (~₹72,000 crore): ICTT at Galathea Bay + Greenfield Airport + Township + Power plant.
CANI submarine optical fibre cable (2020) brought high-speed broadband to major islands for the first time.
Veer Savarkar International Airport, Port Blair, is the primary air link to the mainland.
